parameters.query:
-- Claim a batch of undelivered notifications.
--
-- 'sending' is the claim. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED stops two overlapping runs
-- taking the same row, and the stale-'sending' clause is the recovery path for
-- a run that died between claiming and marking: after the timeout the row is
-- claimable again, exactly like the 15 minute window WF-04 uses on agent_runs.
--
-- attempts is incremented at claim time, not at delivery time. A row that kills
-- the workflow every time it is tried must still run out of attempts, or it
-- blocks the queue forever.
--
-- The parameters are read straight off $1 rather than through a CTE: LIMIT may
-- not reference a variable, so "LIMIT (SELECT ... FROM params)" is rejected.
WITH claimed AS (
    UPDATE notifications
    SET status   = 'sending',
        attempts = notifications.attempts + 1
    WHERE notifications.id IN (
        SELECT n.id
        FROM notifications n
        WHERE n.attempts < ($1::jsonb ->> 'max_attempts')::int
          AND (
                n.status = 'pending'
                -- A retry waits longer each time. Without this the schedule
                -- burns all five attempts in twenty-five minutes, so a Telegram
                -- outage shorter than lunch is enough to drop the day's
                -- notifications on the floor.
             OR (n.status = 'failed'
                 AND n.updated_at < now() - make_interval(
                         mins => n.attempts * ($1::jsonb ->> 'retry_backoff_minutes')::int))
             OR (n.status = 'sending'
                 AND n.updated_at < now() - make_interval(mins => ($1::jsonb ->> 'stale_minutes')::int))
          )
        ORDER BY CASE n.priority WHEN 'immediate' THEN 0 WHEN 'normal' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
                 n.first_seen_at
        LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'batch_size')::int
        FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
    )
    RETURNING notifications.id, notifications.kind, notifications.priority,
              notifications.dedup_key, notifications.title, notifications.body,
              notifications.occurrences, notifications.attempts,
              notifications.first_seen_at, notifications.last_seen_at,
              notifications.company_id
)
SELECT c.id AS notification_id,
       c.kind,
       c.priority,
       c.dedup_key,
       c.title,
       c.body,
       c.occurrences,
       c.attempts,
       c.first_seen_at,
       c.last_seen_at,
       co.name         AS company_name,
       co.domain::text AS company_domain
FROM claimed c
LEFT JOIN companies co ON co.id = c.company_id
ORDER BY CASE c.priority WHEN 'immediate' THEN 0 WHEN 'normal' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
         c.first_seen_at;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ batch_size: Number($env.NOTIFY_BATCH_SIZE || 10), max_attempts: Number($env.NOTIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS || 5), retry_backoff_minutes: Number($env.NOTIFY_RETRY_BACKOFF_MINUTES || 10), stale_minutes: Number($env.NOTIFY_STALE_CLAIM_MINUTES || 10) } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- Close out one delivery. A failure goes back to 'failed', which the outbox
-- index still covers, so the next pass retries it until attempts runs out.
-- After that it stays 'failed' and WF-101 reports it: nothing is lost, but
-- nobody is told twice either.
UPDATE notifications
SET status  = CASE WHEN ($1::jsonb ->> 'delivered')::boolean THEN 'sent' ELSE 'failed' END,
    sent_at = CASE WHEN ($1::jsonb ->> 'delivered')::boolean THEN now() ELSE sent_at END,
    -- The failed status has a CHECK that demands a message, so this must never
    -- resolve to NULL on the failure branch.
    error   = CASE
                  WHEN ($1::jsonb ->> 'delivered')::boolean THEN NULL
                  ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'error', ''), 'delivery failed with no message')
              END
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'notification_id')::uuid
RETURNING id AS notification_id, status, attempts, sent_at, error;
